utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To avoid whatever confusion, I'd like to clearly indicate that although we are still hearing the same case, that we are not hearing at this moment any more the motion filed by the Prosecution to refer the case to Bosnia and Herzegovina under Rule 11 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, but that we move now to a totally different matter, which is a Status Conference in the case which is pending before this Tribunal. I see that the Prosecution has -- well, not completely changed its representatives, but may I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good evening, Your Honour. The Prosecution is represented in this Status Conference by my colleague, Manoj Sachdeva, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, and we have our same case manager, Sebastian van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. Mr. Radovic, you are still here to represent Mr. Stankovic. As you know, at a Status Conference we usually deal with matters such as disclosure but that's not at this moment an issue any more, is it, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We have actually complied with all our disclosure obligation. Of course the Rule 68 disclosure is ongoing and we are still doing searches and will turn over whatever comes up. Otherwise, we are actually trial ready. We have made all our submissions. We have recently filed our motion to suspend all nonessential proceedings pending the transfer motion, and no decision has been taken so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No decision has been taken on that until now. Mr. Radovic, is there any issue in terms of disclosure of the ongoing matter? Has the Defence responded to the motion to suspend further activities?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I know nothing about this motion. I did not receive it. It is possible since communication between the Registry and my office were disrupted because of bad weather, it is quite possible that this motion was not sent to me. I would request that this motion be sent to me, if possible, by e-mail, but in a way that will not compromise the confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was filed already some time ago, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, if I'm not mistaken, it was some two or three weeks ago; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I am actually looking at the motion, but I think it is something like two weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I remember. If there is such a problem with the communication, perhaps, Mr. Radovic, you should look into that, because one or two days' delay one could easily understand, but two weeks, of course is a different matter. There might be the risk that you lose the right to respond to whatever. But I mentioned it because I did not remember to have seen any response to that last motion. Is there anything you'd like to raise at this moment, Mr. Radovic, in respect of the -- in respect of the present situation, apart of course from the 11 bis issue that is pending and on which we have spent quite some time today?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point while the application of the Prosecution under Rule 11 bis for the referral of Mr. Stankovic's case for trial before Bosnia and Herzegovina courts, while that is still pending we will not be making any submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then finally I'd like to inquire into the personal situation of Mr. Stankovic, whether there's -- whether anything has changed or needs specific attention at this moment. Mr. Radovic, I'll first give you an opportunity to say something about that and I'll also give Mr. Stankovic an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the health, I will not be saying anything about that; let Mr. Stankovic say that. I avoided to make any statements about his health at previous Status Conferences because this is his private matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stankovic, if you would like to address me in respect of health or personal circumstances, you're invited to do so at this moment. You also know the conditions: That is, no offensive language, no insults, but if you would like to bring something to my attention please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orie, I would like to ask you not to interrupt me while I speak. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stankovic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me say what I have to say in peace. Please do not interrupt in the middle of my sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stankovic. Mr. Stankovic, I will not -- Mr. Stankovic, I will not interrupt you as long as you keep within the limits I've set. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it comes to my health, you attack my nervous system, you have been doing so on a daily basis for three years. I spend my life waiting for my trial to begin. And today this lady comes here, the representative of this Jamahiriya court, and says the three years do not count. They do not count as being -- having been spent in prison. What do I need to have? To be taken to Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Jamahiriya there, to Iran, to Tehran, to Turkey, and to spend all those years there? People, you have ruined my life. Do you have any evidence? If you do, please go ahead. I want my trial to begin. Please, I want to say something with regard to the referral of the case. It is all the same to me where I will be tried, Mr. Orie. Even if I am to be tried in the Jamahiriya, that's fine. I want to go there to fight them with the facts and arguments and to break them down. But please, they want to turn Viktor Bubanj, which is a notorious execution ground for Serbs and a concentration camp, to turn that into a court and try me there. This reminds me of a statement by George Bush when he says the prison, the camp of Abu Ghraib, where crimes were committed, will be torn down to erase any site of crime and a new camp, new prison, Abu Ghraib will be built there for new crimes. They didn't even tear down this notorious camp in Viktor Bubanj; they just repainted the walls, the walls of the concentration camp that still bear the Serbian blood, that are still speckled with Serbian blood; and this is where I am to be tried. Serbian blood, the blood of innocent civilians, flowed there in rivers, rivers of blood flowed there, people who were taken from the Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stankovic. Mr. Stankovic -- Mr. Stankovic -- Mr. Stankovic. Mr. Stankovic, I gave you an opportunity to say something about your health and your personal circumstances, and I told you not to use offensive language and not to insult anyone. You are at this moment dealing with matters other -- Mr. Stankovic, you are dealing with matters -- Mr. Stankovic, no one will hear you because your microphone is off. Mr. Stankovic, you're dealing at this moment with matters which go beyond your health and your personal circumstances and you are -- well, using language I can still stand but language I -- but language I -- Mr. Stankovic, I've -- Mr. Stankovic, I've given you an opportunity to -- Mr. Stankovic, I've given you an opportunity to express yourself; you have used it in a way which you wasted it. Is there anything else -- is there anything else -- is there anything else counsel would like to -- Mr. Stankovic -- Mr. Stankovic, if -- Mr. Stankovic -- Mr. Stankovic -- Mr. Stankovic, it will not be translated; no one will hear it. Could you please -- Mr. Stankovic, this is my last warning, you'll be removed from this courtroom if you continue. Have you understood this? Mr. Radovic, have you anything to add? I'm sorry, yes, I blocked your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Radovic. Anything you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Nothing arises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This concludes the Status Conference and I would specifically thank the interpreters and the technicians for their assistance at this late moment. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: at 7.10 p.m.
